perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, the available information is:

- He has a close, long-term childhood friendship with Jonathan Balogun. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian had been feeling anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important. He arranged to meet Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something and acting differently. Jonathan admitted Christian was right, said he hadn’t wanted to worry him, and said he was in some trouble and hadn’t known how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag Christian into it. Christian insisted he couldn’t stand by because Jonathan was his best friend. Jonathan said he could use support and resources and needed to figure a way out of the mess.
- Christian came to suspect the trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but said he didn’t do anything illegal himself. Christian said he would look into it discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian found/believed Jonathan was being framed—that someone was trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this. At that point, Christian had some leads but was not sure who was responsible; he planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later determined/believed that the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both knew and trusted. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it and planned to confront that person and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him to be careful, said the person was dangerous, and said he trusted Christian.
- Christian’s own actions include arranging the meeting, confronting Jonathan, offering help, asking about illegal involvement, investigating discreetly, telling Jonathan about the framing, gathering evidence, and planning to confront the culprit.
- The specific identity of the culprit is not named in the dialogue, though Christian claims to have found out who it is.
